questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance
questions.question: A company wants every new resource to have a cost center tag. What is the best approach?
options: Ask users to remember the tag
Use Azure Policy to require the tag or add it automatically
questions.correct_rationale: Policy can deny resources without the tag or add it automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: Reminders are unreliable, and locks and NSGs do not manage tags.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance
questions.question: Which statement about Azure Policy and existing resources is correct?
options: Policies evaluate existing resources for compliance, and remediation tasks can fix some of them
Policies only apply to resources created next year
questions.correct_rationale: Assigned policies scan existing resources and report compliance.
questions.distractor_summary: Policies apply now, do not delete resources, and do see existing resources.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance
questions.question: A regulated company needs a built-in way to check its Azure environment against a standard such as ISO 27001 and track progress. What should it use?
options: The regulatory compliance dashboard in Microsoft Defender for Cloud, using built-in policy initiatives
questions.correct_rationale: Defender for Cloud maps controls to standards using Azure Policy initiatives and shows compliance status.
questions.distractor_summary: The calculator, Virtual Desktop, and locks do not assess compliance standards.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance
questions.question: At which scopes can Azure Policy be assigned?
options: Only at the individual resource level
Only at the tenant root in the portal settings
Only at the virtual network level
Management group, subscription, or resource group
questions.correct_rationale: Policies can be assigned at management group, subscription, or resource group scope and are inherited downward.
questions.distractor_summary: Assignment is not limited to resources, the root only, or virtual networks.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance
questions.question: A company wants to show auditors that sensitive data in Azure storage has been found and labeled. Which service fits?
options: Microsoft Purview data map and classification
questions.correct_rationale: Purview scans data sources and classifies sensitive data.
questions.distractor_summary: Load balancers, virtual networks, and Functions do not classify data.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools in Azure for governance and compliance
questions.question: What does a policy with the Deny effect do?
options: Logs the request and allows it
Prevents a resource request that does not meet the policy from being created or updated
questions.correct_rationale: Deny blocks noncompliant requests at deployment time.
questions.distractor_summary: Audit only logs, policies do not delete afterwards, and they do not bill.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: What is the Azure portal?
options: A command-line tool installed only on Linux
A web-based console for building, managing, and monitoring Azure resources
A physical device for data transfer
questions.correct_rationale: The portal provides a graphical interface for Azure management.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a CLI, a device, or a currency.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: What is Azure Cloud Shell?
options: A browser-based shell that provides Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell without installing anything locally
A desktop app for storage management
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Shell runs in the browser and is already authenticated to Azure.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not Storage Explorer, a gateway, or a backup service.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: Which tools can be used to manage Azure from the command line?
options: Azure Data Box and Azure Migrate
questions.correct_rationale: Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell run commands and scripts against Azure.
questions.distractor_summary: The other pairs are services rather than command-line management tools.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?
options: The deployment and management service that handles every request to create, update, or delete Azure resources
questions.correct_rationale: All management tools send requests through ARM, which authenticates and authorizes them.
questions.distractor_summary: ARM is not a VM size, storage tier, or firewall.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: What are ARM templates?
options: JSON files that declare the resources to deploy, used for infrastructure as code
questions.correct_rationale: ARM templates describe resources declaratively so deployments are repeatable.
questions.distractor_summary: Templates are not screenshots, invoices, or password policies.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: What is Bicep?
options: A language for declaring Azure resources with simpler syntax than JSON ARM templates
questions.correct_rationale: Bicep compiles to ARM templates and is easier to read and write.
questions.distractor_summary: Bicep is not a VM series, dashboard, or support plan.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: A team wants to deploy the same environment repeatedly with identical settings and keep the definition in source control. What should it use?
options: Infrastructure as code with Bicep or ARM templates
Manual clicks in the portal each time
Screenshots stored in a shared folder
A support ticket for each deployment
questions.correct_rationale: Infrastructure as code makes deployments consistent and repeatable.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual steps, screenshots, and tickets are not repeatable deployments.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: Which statement about infrastructure as code with ARM templates or Bicep is correct?
options: They can only deploy virtual machines
They require manual steps for every resource
Deployments are declarative and idempotent, so running the same file again produces the same result
questions.correct_rationale: Declarative templates describe the end state, and repeated deployments converge to it.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not duplicate resources, support many resource types, and avoid manual steps.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: Servers running in another cloud and on premises must appear in the Azure portal and be governed with Azure Policy. What should be used?
questions.correct_rationale: Arc projects outside resources into Azure Resource Manager for management.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Data Box, and Virtual Desktop do not extend management.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: Which statement about the Azure portal is correct?
options: It can only be used on one computer
It requires a separate license for each user
It offers customizable dashboards and is designed for resilience across Azure data centers
questions.correct_rationale: The portal is available from browsers anywhere and supports dashboards.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not tied to one computer, needs no extra license, and shows status.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: An administrator wants to run a quick script against Azure from a borrowed computer without installing tools. What is the best option?
options: Install Azure PowerShell on the borrowed computer
Use Azure Cloud Shell in the browser
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Shell needs only a browser and Azure sign-in.
questions.distractor_summary: Installing tools on a borrowed machine is unnecessary, and the other choices are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: Which interface can be used to manage Azure resources from a mobile device?
questions.correct_rationale: The Azure mobile app lets administrators monitor and manage resources on the go.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not provide mobile management.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: A team needs a consistent way to manage both Azure and on-premises Kubernetes clusters with the same policies. Which service fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Arc-enabled Kubernetes brings outside clusters under Azure management and policy.
questions.distractor_summary: Container Instances runs containers, Blob Storage stores data, and VPN Gateway connects networks.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: Which tool provides an organized way to manage resources by grouping them, applying access control, and tagging, all through one consistent API?
questions.correct_rationale: ARM provides the management layer for grouping, access control, and tags.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not provide the management layer.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What is Azure Advisor?
options: A tool that collects application logs
A dashboard of Azure outages worldwide
A service that analyzes resources and gives recommendations for reliability, security, performance, operational excellence, and cost
questions.correct_rationale: Advisor provides personalized best-practice recommendations in five categories.
questions.distractor_summary: Log collection is Azure Monitor, outage information is Service Health, and invoices come from billing.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What does Azure Service Health provide?
options: Information about Azure service incidents, planned maintenance, and health advisories that affect your resources
A place to write queries on logs
questions.correct_rationale: Service Health includes Azure status, service health for your services, and resource health.
questions.distractor_summary: Recommendations come from Advisor, log queries from Log Analytics, and identity from Entra ID.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What is Azure Monitor?
options: A platform that collects, analyzes, and acts on metrics and logs from Azure, on-premises, and other cloud resources
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Monitor gathers telemetry and supports alerts, dashboards, and analysis.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not storage redundancy, licensing, or a CDN.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What is Log Analytics in Azure Monitor?
options: A tool for writing and running queries on log data collected by Azure Monitor
A physical log book in the data center
questions.correct_rationale: Log Analytics runs queries over logs in a workspace for analysis.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not physical, a cost estimator, or networking.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What does Application Insights provide?
options: Monitoring of web application performance, availability, and usage
questions.correct_rationale: Application Insights, part of Azure Monitor, tracks application telemetry such as requests and failures.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not provide firewalls, binary storage, or identities.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: Administrators want an email when a VM's CPU stays above 90 percent for 15 minutes. What should they configure?
options: An Azure Monitor metric alert with an action group
questions.correct_rationale: Metric alerts evaluate conditions and use action groups to send notifications.
questions.distractor_summary: Policies, locks, and budgets do not watch CPU usage.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: A company wants to know if a recent Azure platform outage affected its own resources. Which tool should it check?
questions.correct_rationale: Service Health shows incidents for the services and regions you use.
questions.distractor_summary: Advisor recommends improvements, the calculator estimates costs, and Arc extends management.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: Which component of Azure Service Health shows the health of individual resources, such as a specific VM?
questions.correct_rationale: Resource health reports on individual resources, while Azure status covers global service health.
questions.distractor_summary: Azure status is global, Advisor recommends, and Application Insights monitors apps.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: A team wants to find which web pages in its app load slowly and which external calls fail. Which tool fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: Application Insights shows request times, dependencies, and failures for applications.
questions.distractor_summary: Service Health reports platform incidents, Advisor cost advice is unrelated, and Policy checks compliance.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What is an action group in Azure Monitor?
options: A group of users with Owner rights
A collection of notification and automation actions, such as email, SMS, or running a runbook, triggered by alerts
questions.correct_rationale: Action groups define what happens when an alert fires.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not role groups, networks, or storage settings.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: An operations team wants a single dashboard that shows metrics from several resources. What should they use?
options: Azure Monitor workbooks or Azure portal dashboards
questions.correct_rationale: Workbooks and dashboards combine metrics and logs into one view.
questions.distractor_summary: The other choices are unrelated to visualization of monitoring data.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: Which category is one of the Azure Advisor recommendation categories?
questions.correct_rationale: Advisor's categories are reliability, security, performance, operational excellence, and cost.
questions.distractor_summary: The other choices are not Advisor categories.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: Logs from VMs, apps, and Azure activity must be kept in one place and searched together. What should be configured?
options: Store logs only on each VM's local disk
Send the data to a Log Analytics workspace and query it with Kusto Query Language
questions.correct_rationale: A shared workspace centralizes logs for queries across sources.
questions.distractor_summary: Local disks scatter logs, emails do not scale, and locks are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: Which data types does Azure Monitor primarily collect?
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Monitor's core data types are numeric metrics and log records.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not collect invoices, secrets, or serial numbers as core data.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: A team wants to review the activity log to find who deleted a resource yesterday. What does the activity log provide?
options: A record of subscription-level control plane operations, including who performed them and when
The contents of every file in a storage account
The CPU usage of each VM
questions.correct_rationale: The activity log tracks create, update, and delete operations and the caller.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not store file contents, CPU metrics, or invoices.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What does Azure Advisor's reliability category help with?
options: Ensuring and improving the continuity of business-critical applications
questions.correct_rationale: Reliability recommendations help keep applications available and resilient.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost is a separate category, and code and domains are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: A company wants to be notified ahead of planned Azure maintenance that may affect its VMs. Which tool supports this?
options: Azure Service Health alerts for planned maintenance
questions.correct_rationale: Service Health can alert on planned maintenance events for your resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost alerts, the calculator, and Storage Explorer do not report maintenance.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: Which tool gives a global view of the health of all Azure services across all regions?
questions.correct_rationale: The Azure status page shows widespread service incidents across regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Resource health is per resource, Application Insights monitors apps, and Policy checks compliance.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: A web app must alert when its home page fails to load from several locations around the world. What should be configured?
options: A resource lock on the app
Availability tests in Application Insights with alerts
questions.correct_rationale: Availability tests check endpoints from multiple locations and alert on failures.
questions.distractor_summary: Locks, policy, and storage lifecycle rules do not test availability.

questions.subdomain: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
questions.question: What does Azure Monitor's VM insights provide?
options: Performance and dependency monitoring of virtual machines, including processes and connections
questions.correct_rationale: VM insights shows VM performance trends and maps dependencies.
questions.distractor_summary: Encryption, licensing, and DNS are other services.

questions.subdomain: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
questions.question: A company wants to preview what a Bicep deployment will change before running it. What should it use?
options: The what-if operation for the deployment
questions.correct_rationale: What-if shows the resources that will be created, changed, or deleted before the deployment runs.
questions.distractor_summary: Locks, Service Health, and the TCO calculator do not preview deployments.

questions.subdomain: Describe cost management in Azure
questions.question: What is a savings plan for compute in Azure?
options: A free monthly allowance for every subscription
A commitment to spend a fixed hourly amount on compute for one or three years in exchange for discounted prices across eligible services
A way to avoid paying for data transfer
questions.correct_rationale: Savings plans trade a spend commitment for lower prices, with more flexibility than reservations across services and regions.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not free allowances, redundancy options, or data transfer waivers.
